profile.err.co_conflict: Curve Optimizer: choose either an all-core setting or per-core settings.
profile.err.dynamic_boost_conflict: The preset contains conflicting Dynamic Boost instructions.
info.GpuCoreOffsetMhz:
Shifts the GPU clock curve by a common offset. Positive adds clock at the same voltage anchors; negative reduces clock.

Too much offset can cause artifacts or driver crashes. Tune in small steps and check under load. A custom V/F curve and a global clock offset are mutually exclusive.
info.GpuMemoryOffsetMhz:
Raises or lowers the VRAM clock. More memory bandwidth can help when the GPU is memory-limited.

An excessive offset can cause artifacts, instability or lower performance. After each change, check that the tuning actually improves performance and remains stable.
info.GpuVfCurve:
Edits the target clock at the GPU's existing voltage anchors. A common use is undervolting: tune a suitable clock at a lower voltage anchor.

The anchors stay fixed; the curve does not enforce a hard voltage ceiling. Boost and stability still depend on the GPU, load and driver. Replaces the global GPU clock offset.
info.MaxFan:
Requests the HP BIOS Max-Fan override for both fans. This adds cooling headroom under load, at noticeably higher noise.

Off only releases this override. It does not confirm a safe handover to BIOS automatic control.
info.GpuPowerLimitMw:
Sets the NVIDIA driver's offered power limit in watts. Bounds and the configured original must be readable so the app can verify and restore the change.

That original query is unavailable on the reference laptop, so this control remains unavailable there. A reported limit is not measured power draw.
info.GpuUnleashed: Turns NVIDIA Dynamic Boost on or off through the HP PPAB flag. The GPU may receive additional power within the shared CPU/GPU budget. Achievable wattage also depends on performance mode, AC adapter, temperature and firmware. Sustained 115 W has not yet been confirmed by a load test.
info.CpuTemperatureLimitC:
Sets the CPU's Tctl temperature limit. When the CPU reaches it, boost is constrained.

A lower value can reduce cooling demand and chassis heat at the cost of sustained performance. A higher value does not guarantee extra performance. The offered range is not a stability guarantee.
info.CpuStapmLimitMw: Legacy STAPM instruction. Independent STAPM control is not enabled in this app; use the supported Slow/PPT limits instead.
info.CpuSlowPptLimitMw:
Sets the CPU's Slow power limit through the app's SMU path. Together with PPT, current and temperature limits, it constrains sustained load.

A lower value can keep sustained loads cooler. More watts add boost headroom only when another limit is not already binding. Application is blocked while the original HP controller is active.
info.CpuPptLimitMw:
Sets the CPU's Package Power Tracking (PPT) limit. It works together with Slow, TDC/EDC and the temperature limit.

More watts can add boost headroom; fewer watts reduce the power budget. Actual performance depends on load, cooling and other limits. Application is blocked while the original HP controller is active.
info.CpuTdcMa:
Sets the sustained CPU current limit, TDC, in amperes. It constrains boost alongside power and temperature limits.

Less current can reduce VRM load. A higher limit does not guarantee a higher clock; the offered bounds do not certify stable sustained operation.
info.CpuEdcMa:
Sets the CPU's EDC current limit for short load spikes, in amperes. A tight limit can constrain boost.

A higher value alone does not guarantee extra performance. Power limits, cooling and stability still matter.
info.CpuPboScalar:
Sets the PBO scalar, which affects how boost uses its voltage and time margins.

Higher values can increase power and heat without a measurable performance gain. 1× was tested on the reference device; the entire offered range is not qualified as stable operation.
info.CpuBoostProfile: Legacy boost profile. This separate AMD control path is not implemented. Windows processor boost and EPP provide the supported boost-tuning policies.
info.CpuCurveOptimizerAllCore:
Adjusts the CPU voltage/frequency curve for all cores together. Values are Curve Optimizer steps, not fixed millivolts.

Negative values can improve efficiency and boost. Overly aggressive values may become unstable even at idle or light load. Check small changes under load and in everyday use.
info.CpuCurveOptimizerPerCore:
Tunes Curve Optimizer for each core separately. Undervolting headroom varies between cores; the fastest core does not automatically have the most margin.

Values are steps, not fixed mV. All-core and per-core settings cannot be included in the same preset.
info.CpuAllCoreVoltageOffsetMv: Direct all-core voltage offset in mV. This control path is not enabled. Curve Optimizer uses its own steps and is not a fixed mV offset.
info.AmdCpuVoltageMv: Fixed CPU voltage for manual OC. This control path is not enabled in the current app.
info.AmdCpuClockMhz: Fixed CPU clock for manual OC. This control path is not enabled in the current app.
info.IntelPl1Mw: Intel sustained power limit (PL1). The Intel hardware adapter is not implemented yet; the field alone does not enable application.
info.IntelPl2Mw: Intel short-term power limit (PL2). The Intel hardware adapter is not implemented yet.
info.IntelPl4Mw: Intel peak power limit (PL4). The Intel hardware adapter is not implemented yet.
info.IntelIccMaxMa: Intel ICC Max current limit. The Intel hardware adapter is not implemented yet.
info.IntelCpuPowerBalance: Intel power-budget weighting between the CPU and iGPU. The Intel hardware adapter is not implemented yet.
info.IntelCacheVoltageOffsetMv: Intel CPUs: voltage offset for the cache in millivolts. Negative saves power, too negative causes crashes.
info.IntelSystemAgentVoltageOffsetMv: Intel CPUs: voltage offset for the system agent (memory controller and I/O) in millivolts.
info.IntelCoreRatios: Intel CPUs: turbo multipliers by number of active cores, comma separated (e.g. 48, 47, 46). Clock = multiplier × 100 MHz.
info.WindowsBoostMode:
Chooses the Windows power plan's processor boost policy.

Disabled does not request boost above base clock. Enabled and Aggressive allow more boost; the efficient variants put more weight on energy use. Actual CPU behavior also depends on the driver, firmware and other limits.
info.WindowsMinimumProcessorPercent:
Sets the Windows plan's minimum processor state in percent. This is a performance policy, not a measured clock.

A higher value can affect responsiveness and idle power. The actual effect depends on the system.
info.WindowsMaximumProcessorPercent:
Sets the Windows plan's maximum processor state in percent. This is a policy, not a fixed clock target.

Values below 100% can constrain performance and, depending on the system, boost. Use Processor boost when you specifically want to disable boost.
info.WindowsProcessorEppPercent:
Energy Performance Preference balances performance and efficiency.

0% favors performance; 100% favors efficiency. It does not set a fixed clock or power draw. Useful when tuning a balanced or battery preset.
info.WindowsCoreParkingMinPercent:
Sets the Windows policy's minimum share of unparked cores. Higher values allow less core parking and can increase idle power.

This is not a live count of active cores; Windows and CPU firmware determine actual behavior.
info.WindowsCoreParkingMaxPercent:
Sets the Windows policy's maximum share of unparked cores. A lower value can constrain available multicore performance.

This is a policy, not a measurement of active cores.
info.CpuCcdAffinity:
Selects CCDs for the foreground program: 1 = first CCD, 2 = second CCD, 3 = both. The app's helper applies process affinity and retains the original assignment.

A single CCD can change a game's behavior but reduces the available cores. Protected programs, such as those with anti-cheat, may reject the change.
info.WindowsEnergyMode:
Chooses the Windows power mode between efficiency, balanced and performance.

The Balanced power plan must be active or selected in the same preset. Power mode and power plan are separate settings.
info.WindowsPowerPlan:
Changes the active Windows power plan. The app preserves the original selection and, where relevant, the target plan's CPU policies.

A plan name alone does not guarantee a particular clock or power draw.
info.DisplayRefreshRateHz:
Chooses an offered refresh rate for the primary Windows display. Higher Hz can make motion smoother; lower Hz can reduce power use.

Only currently available display modes are used.
info.GraphicsMode:
Stores the BIOS boot preference for graphics mode (MUX). Hybrid, discrete GPU and, where offered, integrated GPU are separate preferences.

The change needs a restart. Reading back the BIOS value does not confirm actual display routing or a powered-off NVIDIA GPU. Physical switching and iGPU-only battery operation still need validation.

curve.help:
GPU curve
Drag: move a point or the selected range vertically.
Shift + drag point: move the loaded base curve/selection.
Alt + drag point: move the current draft/selection evenly.
Ctrl + drag point: tilt the curve around the opposite end point.
Shift + drag in empty chart: select a voltage range.
Shift + Left/Right: extend the selection. Ctrl + A: all points.
Shift + Enter: flatten the selection; without one, plateau from the point.
Esc or double-click: clear the selection; Esc while dragging: cancel.

Common controls
Left/Right: choose a point. Up/Down: 1 MHz or 1 %.
Ctrl + Up/Down: 10 steps. Enter: edit the number field.
Ctrl + Z: undo. Ctrl + Y / Ctrl + Shift + Z: redo.
Ctrl + D: reset to the loaded draft. Ctrl + S: save profile.
Mouse wheel or +/−: zoom voltage/temperature. Ctrl: Y axis.
Shift + mouse wheel: scroll horizontally. Ctrl + 0: whole curve.

Fans
Ctrl + Left/Right: edit temperature. Shift: larger steps.
Right-click: add or delete a point. Ins: add point. Del: remove point.
One shared curve applies to CPU and GPU fans; saving hands it to the fan service.

The GPU curve is applied through a preset.
Fixed voltage/clock lock and OC Scanner are not available yet.
